title: Equivariant Elliptic Index and Character Formula

items.title: Equivariant elliptic-complex index and character
items.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, where $r\ge0$ is an integer, be a compact torus and $M$ a compact smooth manifold without boundary. A smooth left $T$-action is a jointly smooth map $a:T\times M\to M$ with $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(st,x)=a(s,a(t,x))$. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank complex vector bundles on $M$. For each $j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be a linear differential operator of finite order $m_j$, and put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$. In local coordinates and bundle frames, if $d_j=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m_j}a_{j,\alpha}(x)\partial_x^\alpha$, use the positive-frequency principal symbol $\sigma(d_j)(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=m_j}a_{j,\alpha}(x)(i\xi)^\alpha$. The sequence is a complex when $d_{j+1}d_j=0$ for every $j$. It is **elliptic** when, for every $x\in M$ and every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi\in T_x^*M$, the sequence of principal-symbol maps

$$0\longrightarrow E_x^0\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_0)(x,\xi)}E_x^1\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_1)(x,\xi)}\cdots\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_{N-1})(x,\xi)}E_x^N\longrightarrow0$$

is exact. Suppose each bundle has a $T$-linearization: a jointly smooth map $T\times E^j\to E^j$ whose restrictions $\rho_t^j(x):E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$ are complex-linear isomorphisms, with $\rho_e^j(x)=I_{E_x^j}$ and $\rho_{st}^j(x)=\rho_s^j(t\cdot x)\circ\rho_t^j(x)$. The induced section maps

$$ (U_t^j s)(x):=\rho_t^j(t^{-1}\cdot x)\bigl(s(t^{-1}\cdot x)\bigr) $$

commute with $d_j$. Require the cohomology spaces $H^j(E^\bullet):=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ to be finite-dimensional. The representation ring $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of $T$. Define

$$\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j[H^j(E^\bullet)]\in R(T),\qquad \chi_{E^\bullet}(t):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}\!\left(U_t^j\bigm|_{H^j(E^\bullet)}\right).$$

For a two-term complex $0\to C^\infty(M,E^+)\xrightarrow{D^+}C^\infty(M,E^-)\to0$, this gives $[\ker D^+]-[\operatorname{coker}D^+]$. This definition concerns elliptic complexes, not transversally elliptic operators.

items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, $n=\dim M>0$, and $E$ a finite-rank Hermitian bundle. Let $P:C^\infty(M,E)\to C^\infty(M,E)$ be a smooth second-order differential operator. In local coordinates and a bundle frame, write $P=\sum_{|\alpha|\le2}a_\alpha(x)\partial_x^\alpha$ and define its positive-frequency principal symbol by $p(x,\xi)=\sum_{|\alpha|=2}a_\alpha(x)(i\xi)^\alpha$ (equivalently, the coefficient of $\lambda^2$ in $e^{-i\lambda f}P(e^{i\lambda f}v)$ at $df_x=\xi$). Suppose $p(x,\xi)$ is a Hermitian matrix satisfying $p(x,\xi)\ge c|\xi|^2I$ for some $c>0$. Assume its nonnegative selfadjoint realization has a complete orthonormal basis of smooth eigensections and a smooth heat kernel $K_t(y,z):E_z\to E_y$ relative to Riemannian volume. No scalar-principal-symbol hypothesis is imposed. In normal coordinates and smooth unitary frames based at $x$, set

$$k_x(w)=(2\pi)^{-n}\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{iw\cdot\xi}e^{-p(x,\xi)}\,d\xi.$$

Then $k_x$ is Schwartz, $\int k_x(w)\,dw=I$, and, locally uniformly for bounded $a,b\in T_xM$,

$$t^{n/2}K_t(\exp_x(\sqrt t\,a),\exp_x(\sqrt t\,b))\longrightarrow k_x(a-b).$$

For every integer $L>n$ there is $C_L$ such that

$$\|K_t(y,z)\|\le C_Lt^{-n/2}(1+d(y,z)/\sqrt t)^{-L}\qquad(0<t\le1).$$

In dimension zero the corresponding assertion is the finite-dimensional limit $K_t(x,x)\to I$ and zero kernel between distinct points.

items.title: Relative tangent-groupoid heat-trace limit at simple fixed points
items.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, $r\ge0$, be a compact torus acting smoothly by isometries on a compact Riemannian manifold $M$ without boundary. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank Hermitian bundles and, for $0\le j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be first-order differential maps with $d_{j+1}d_j=0$. Assume the principal-symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero real cotangent vector. Suppose a jointly smooth unitary bundle action has fiber maps $\rho_t^j(x):E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$ satisfy $\rho_e^j(x)=I_{E_x^j}$ and $\rho_{st}^j(x)=\rho_s^j(t\cdot x)\circ\rho_t^j(x)$; on sections set $(U_t^j s)(y)=\rho_t^j(t^{-1}\cdot y)(s(t^{-1}\cdot y))$ and require $U_t^{j+1}d_j=d_jU_t^j$. Put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$, $E^{\mathrm{ev}}=\bigoplus_{j\text{ even}}E^j$, $E^{\mathrm{odd}}=\bigoplus_{j\text{ odd}}E^j$, $d=\bigoplus_jd_j$, and $\Delta=(d+d^*)^2$, where $d^*$ is the formal adjoint for the chosen metrics and Riemannian volume. For the nonnegative selfadjoint Hodge realization on $L^2$, assume that $\Delta$ has discrete spectrum, smooth eigensections, a trace-class heat operator $e^{-t\Delta}$ with smooth kernel for every $t>0$, finite-dimensional cohomology, and a harmonic representative for each cohomology class. For $g\in T$, let $M^g=\{x\in M:g\cdot x=x\}$, and suppose each $x\in M^g$ is simple, meaning $I-dg_x:T_xM\to T_xM$ is invertible. Then

$$\lim_{t\downarrow0}\operatorname{Str}(U_g e^{-t\Delta})=\sum_{x\in M^g}\frac{\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}(\rho_g^j|_{E_x^j})}{|\det_{\mathbb R}(I-dg_x)|}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Str}$ is the trace on $E^{\mathrm{ev}}$ minus the trace on $E^{\mathrm{odd}}$. The simplicity condition makes $M^g$ a finite set; the determinant is the normal Jacobian at that isolated fixed point.

items.title: Equivariant elliptic-complex index character and fixed-component formula
items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$, $r\ge0$, act smoothly by isometries on a compact smooth manifold $M$ without boundary. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be smooth finite-rank Hermitian complex bundles and $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ first-order differential maps with $d_{j+1}d_j=0$, setting $d_{-1}=d_N=0$. Their positive-frequency symbols use $\partial_x^\alpha\mapsto(i\xi)^\alpha$. Assume the symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero real cotangent vector. A jointly smooth unitary bundle action has maps $\rho_t^j(x):E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$, with $\rho_e^j(x)=I$ and $\rho_{st}^j(x)=\rho_s^j(t\cdot x)\rho_t^j(x)$; set $(U_t^js)(x)=\rho_t^j(t^{-1}\cdot x)s(t^{-1}\cdot x)$ and require $U_t^{j+1}d_j=d_jU_t^j$.

Write $d=\bigoplus_jd_j$, let $d^*$ be its formal adjoint for the invariant metrics and Riemannian volume, and put $D=d+d^*$. Its even-to-odd symbol defines the compact-support class $\sigma\in K^0_{T,c}(T^*M)$. The cohomology groups $H^j=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ are finite dimensional. Define $\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet)=\sum_j(-1)^j[H^j]\in R(T)$, where $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations.

For any $g\in T$, write $M^g=\coprod_aF_a$ for its finitely many connected fixed components, $\nu_a=(TF_a)^\perp\subset TM|_{F_a}$, $\pi_a:T^*F_a\to F_a$, and $i_a:T^*F_a\hookrightarrow T^*M$ for extension of covectors by zero on $\nu_a$. Put $\nu_{a,\mathbb C}=\nu_a\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ and $e_a=\lambda_{-1}(\nu_{a,\mathbb C}^*)=\sum_k(-1)^k[\Lambda^k\nu_{a,\mathbb C}^*]$. Then

$$\chi_{\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet)}(g)=\sum_a\int_{T^*F_a}\frac{\operatorname{ch}_{g,c}(i_a^*\sigma)}{\pi_a^*\operatorname{ch}_g(e_a)}\,\pi_a^*\operatorname{Td}(TF_a\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C).$$

For a symbol on the $g$-fixed base, $\operatorname{ch}_{g,c}$ means the compact-support relative Chern character weighted by the eigenvalue of $g$ on each eigenbundle; for an absolute virtual bundle $V$, $\operatorname{ch}_g(V)=\sum_\lambda\lambda\operatorname{ch}(V_\lambda)$. The Todd class is $\prod_jx_j/(1-e^{-x_j})$ in formal Chern roots, truncated in each degree. The integral is the oriented compact-support cohomological pairing on the cotangent bundle, oriented by $d\theta=\sum_jd\xi_j\wedge dx_j$. The denominator has nonzero degree-zero term $\det_{\mathbb R}(I-dg|_{\nu_a})$, so its positive-degree part is inverted by a finite nilpotent series. Its full characteristic class is retained for a positive-dimensional component. The degree-zero value of $\operatorname{ch}_g$ is the trace at $g$; it is distinct from the degree-zero rank of a Borel equivariant Chern character.

At an element where the fixed locus changes, the formula uses that element's actual fixed components and normal bundles. It applies also at $g=e$, when $F=M$ and the normal denominator is $1$; it asserts no transversally elliptic distribution formula. If the fixed components are isolated points, it specializes to

$$\chi_{\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet)}(g)=\sum_{x\in M^g}\frac{\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}(\rho_g^j(x)|_{E_x^j})}{|\det_{\mathbb R}(I-dg_x)|}.$$

This isolated-point assertion also holds assuming only countable choice, provided every fixed point is simple and the nonnegative selfadjoint Hodge realization of $\Delta=D^2$ has discrete spectrum, smooth eigensections, trace-class heat operators with smooth kernels for positive time, finite-dimensional cohomology, and zero eigenspace canonically isomorphic to that cohomology. Thus the earlier spectral isolated-point case retains its weaker choice assumption.

title: Equivariant Elliptic Index and Character Formula — Examples

items.title: A nontrivial virtual character on a two-point manifold
items.statement: Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and let $M=\{p,q\}$ be a two-point smooth $0$-manifold with trivial $T$-action. For $k\in\mathbb Z$, let $\mathbb C_k$ be the one-dimensional representation $[s]\mapsto e^{2\pi i k s}$. Take the zero-differential complex whose fibers are $E_p^0=\mathbb C_0\oplus\mathbb C_1$, $E_p^1=\mathbb C_2$, $E_q^0=\mathbb C_1$, and $E_q^1=\mathbb C_0$, with all other fibers zero. Its equivariant index is $2[\mathbb C_1]-[\mathbb C_2]$, with character $2z-z^2$ at $z=e^{2\pi i s}$. Every point is fixed, the tangent determinant is the empty determinant $1$, and the fixed-point sum is also $2z-z^2$.

items.title: The de Rham index character of a rotating two-sphere
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Give $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$ its outward orientation and the complexified de Rham complex $E^j=\Lambda^jT^*S^2\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, with differential $d_{\mathbb C}(\alpha+i\beta)=d\alpha+i\,d\beta$. Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act by rotation through angle $2\pi s$ about the $z$-axis for $[s]\in T$. For every nonidentity $g=[s]$, the fixed set consists of the north and south poles. The de Rham index character is $2$, and the two isolated fixed-point contributions are each $1$.
